doc: The compact stop card — the unit Nearby and Favourites are both lists of — as rules over the canonical model. These six derivations lived inside `apps/mobile`'s components until WP4-0 and were reachable only by rendering a React tree, so nothing could assert them and a second renderer would have had to re-implement each one by reading JSX. That is the drift Wave 4 exists to disprove, and a re-implementation would have PASSED a byte-identity check on the day it was written while proving the opposite. Every `args` below is verbatim from the dataset build `d598893de6add2e4` of 2026-07-29 — real place ids, real member poles, real ALL-CAPS names with operator codes, real GMB "Scheduled" remarks in all three locales — because the shapes that break these rules (a place with no live readings, a reading with no destination, a blank `en`) are ones nobody invents. Arrival timestamps are the one synthetic part, stated against a fixed `nowIso` of 2026-07-29T11:50:30+08:00: a fixture that read a clock would be worthless to a second platform and flaky on the first. Absent optional values are JSON `null` on both sides, per `test/corpus.ts` — stated rather than omitted, so a Swift or Kotlin port comparing structs has nothing to guess. The expectations were derived from the implementation only AFTER a parity harness proved it equal to the shipped components over 120 real rows in 3 locales, with exactly one declared difference: the imminence band moves 360 s → 180 s, because `EtaBadge` carried a literal `value <= 5` while the served `warnUnderSec` said 180. That row is `the-urgency-bands-at-every-boundary`.

displayName.doc: How a bus-stop name is rendered anywhere in the product (ADR-034): title-cased, with the operator's own pole code split off so a renderer can set it smaller. Two operations in a fixed order — the code comes off first, so it is never cased.

cases.name: an-all-caps-kmb-name-with-a-pole-code
cases.why: The everyday KMB shape, verbatim from the build. Both halves at once, and the ORDER matters: the code is split off before title-casing, so "ST935" survives intact. Title-casing first yields "St935", which reads as a typo rather than a code.

cases.name: a-mixed-case-name-is-left-alone
cases.why: Citybus and GMB already write names for humans, so `titleCaseName` must not touch them — "outside" must not become "Outside".

cases.why: Absent, not empty string — a renderer draws the code slot only when there is one, and `''` would put an empty span at a different size into every row.

cases.name: a-circular-marker-is-not-a-pole-code
cases.why: Real and a genuine trap: "(Circular)" sits exactly where a pole code sits, so `splitStopCode` takes it as one. Recorded as the behaviour that ships — `stripCircular` is the separate rule for route names, and conflating them would strip a real code like "(ST311)" from a stop.

stopCardCaption.doc: The caption under a stop name: a compass direction for a merged place, then distance · walk. Two separators that are not interchangeable, and either part may be absent — Favourites shows no distance, a lone stop has no bearing. Both absent yields the empty string, which is the signal to draw no caption line at all.

cases.name: merged-place-shows-direction-then-distance-and-walk
cases.why: Both parts, and the reason the separators are not interchangeable: `' · '` binds the distance to its own walk time, `'  ·  '` (wider) separates that pair from the compass direction, because they are different kinds of fact. A second renderer re-deriving this gets a plausible caption with the wrong rhythm and nothing fails.

cases.name: the-same-caption-in-traditional-chinese
cases.why: The words are localised and the punctuation is not. Pins that a port does not "translate" the separators, and that the order does not flip.

cases.name: a-lone-stop-has-no-mean-bearing
cases.why: Only merged places carry a travel bearing (ADR-042), so a GMB pole shows distance alone — and crucially with NO leading separator, which a naive join produces.

cases.name: favourites-passes-no-distance
cases.why: The Favourites list shows the same card without a distance, so the direction must stand alone with no TRAILING separator. This is the half a renderer forgets, because Nearby never exercises it.

cases.name: neither-part-means-no-caption-at-all
cases.why: Empty string, not " · " or a stray space: it is the signal to draw no caption line, so anything non-empty puts an empty row on screen.

cases.name: standing-at-the-stop-reads-zero-metres
cases.why: Real: the query point was the place centroid, so `distanceM` was 1 and `formatDistance` rounds to the nearest 10 m — "0m". Recorded rather than fixed, because it is `geo#formatDistance`'s pinned behaviour and "0m · 1 min walk" is at least not wrong. A port must reproduce it or the two disagree at the one distance every rider sees when they arrive.

stopCardView.doc: One whole card: the name split for display, the caption, the route rows under the served `maxRows` cap, and the "+N more" count — computed together with the cap, because they are one rule and a caller that pre-sliced its list made the count zero. Each row carries where the service is headed, its soonest arrival split into figure and unit, whether that reading is stale, and how much attention it is owed as a NAME rather than a colour (ADR-053). Since WP5-9 the readings arrive one per line per BOARDING POLE, and a compact card has no kerb heading to make that legible, so they are collapsed to one row per rider line (first sighting, which is the soonest because every producer serves this list soonest-first) BEFORE the cap — and `routeCount` is a count of lines, so both sides of the "+N more" subtraction are in the same unit.

cases.name: merged-place-caps-thirteen-readings-at-six-and-offers-twenty-more
cases.why: The everyday case, verbatim from the build of 2026-07-29: Belair Garden southwest kerb, 5 member poles, 26 routes, 13 of them with a live reading. Six rows and "+20 more" — the cap and the count are one rule, and a caller that pre-sliced its list computed 4−4=0 and lost the affordance entirely (the shipped Favourites bug WP3-4 found).

cases.name: the-urgency-bands-at-every-boundary
cases.why: THE ROW THIS MODULE WAS WRITTEN FOR. One card, eight readings, at −61/−60/−1/59/60/179/180/359 s. `none` past the symmetric due band, `due` inside it either side of zero, `soon` under `warnUnderSec`, `normal` above. The 180 s and 359 s rows are the witnesses to a real disagreement: `EtaBadge` used a literal `value <= 5` (360 s) while the served `warnUnderSec` was 180, so 7 of 40 rows in a live sample were coloured imminent against the policy. Urgency is a NAME, never a colour — each platform maps `soon` through its own colour system (ADR-053). `maxRows` is lifted to 8 here so every band is visible in one row of the corpus; the cap itself is pinned by the two cases above.

cases.why: Measured live on 2026-07-31 and the reason this rule exists. GMB 68K boards at BOTH poles of Fu Kin Street and `/v1/etas` now publishes a reading for each (WP5-9) — 9 minutes at GMB:20015749, 15 at GMB:20015724. A compact card has no kerb heading, so two rows reading `68K → Julimount Garden` would ask a rider to choose with nothing to choose by; the kerb is a Place-detail fact and this card shows the line, soonest first. The count is the half that would have gone quietly wrong: `routeCount` is 2 rider LINES at this place (68K outbound and 68S inbound), so a card showing 2 pole-rows would have said '+0 more' and hidden 68S entirely. nearbyView.doc: Nearby's list: every card, nearest first. The wire promises no order, so the sort is a rule — and it is stable, so a tie keeps the response order rather than shuffling between renderers.

cases.name: nearest-first-whatever-order-the-response-arrived-in
cases.why: THE ORDERING IS A RULE, not a formality: `/v1/nearby`'s schema describes `distanceM` and promises nothing about sequence, so a renderer iterating the response as received produces a different list — and only sometimes, which is the worst kind of divergence. Here the four real Belair cards are fed in reverse.
